scenes.title: Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

steps.title: Set steps 2 to 4
steps.caption: Hold step 2 (2,4), tap and release step 4 (4,4), then release step 2. The range is now steps 2 to 4 and those steps brighten. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: the channel loops D, E, F (62, 64, 65). Tap Play again to stop.

steps.title: Refuse an end before the start
steps.caption: Hold step 4 (4,4), tap step 2 (2,4), then release step 2 and step 4. The end would come before the start, so Mosaic refuses it: the footer reads End must follow start and the grid still shows steps 2 to 4.

steps.title: Refuse a start released first
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and Stop to check: it still loops D, E, F, because the refused gesture changed nothing. Then press step 2 (2,4), press step 4 (4,4) and release step 2 before step 4. The order of release matters: the footer reads End must follow start again and steps 2 to 4 stay bright. To set a range, release the later step first.

steps.title: Still D, E, F
steps.caption: Tap Play and listen: D, E, F (62, 64, 65) loop with the same timing, because neither refused gesture altered the range. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Choose a valid range
steps.caption: Hold step 3 (3,4), tap and release step 4 (4,4), then release step 3. Steps 3 and 4 are bright and steps 1, 2 and 5 are dark: a correctly ordered gesture is accepted again.

steps.title: Hear the new range
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: E and F (64, 65) loop with the same step timing and gate lengths. Tap Play again to stop.

scenes.title: Mute a channel and bring a running phrase back

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. No channel is muted, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

steps.title: Select channel 1 without muting
steps.caption: Press channel button (1,1) and let go after about half a second, well before one second is up. A short press only selects the channel, so the button stays bright and nothing is muted.

steps.title: Hear channel one
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: channel 1 plays C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65), and the strip below lists the four notes. Tap Play again to stop.

steps.title: Mute with a long press
steps.caption: Hold (1,1) for a full second, then let go. The button dims to show channel 1 is muted; a muted channel still counts as selected.

steps.title: Listen to the muted channel
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen for about a second and a half: the dimmed channel sends no notes, and the strip below stays empty. Playback keeps running, so the other channels would carry on.

steps.title: Unmute with K1
steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens again, so channel 1 is unmuted.

steps.title: Hear it again
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8): with channel 1 unmuted, C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65) sound again. Tap Play to stop.

steps.title: Mute while it plays
steps.caption: Tap Play. While the phrase sounds, hold (1,1) for a full second: the button dims and the notes stop. The clock keeps running, but no new notes sound for the next second and a half.

steps.title: Bring channel one back
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens and the phrase comes back in time with the running pattern, picking up wherever the loop has reached rather than starting over.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. Nothing is assigned to Trig params yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.

steps.title: Give Chord Note Strum a slot
steps.caption: Open Trig params (E1 to the channel's Trig params page), press K2 to enter the slot list, turn E3 until the parameter reads Chord Note Strum, press K3 to assign it to the first slot, then press K2 to leave the list. The slot shows as Strm on the screen: it is the strum slot.

steps.title: A new slot starts at X
steps.caption: Press K3 to select the Strm slot. It reads X, which means no strum: the notes of a chord sound together. Every strum division is chosen with E3 from here.

steps.title: First supported division
steps.caption: Turn E3 left a few detents: nothing happens, because X is the lowest value. Then turn E3 one detent right. The slot reads 1/24, one twenty-fourth of a channel step between chord notes, the smallest strum division.

steps.title: Climb to the upper bound
steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right, about ninety detents, through the supported divisions until the slot reads 128 channel steps, then turn a few detents further: it stays at 128 and extra turns do not go higher.

steps.title: One step back down
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent left. The slot reads 120, the next supported division below 128; turning back left continues down towards 1/24 and X.

scenes.title: Use the first and last Trig params slots

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. No Trig params slot is assigned yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to slot 1
steps.caption: Open Trig params, press K2 to enter the slot list and turn E3 to CC 1, press K3, then K2. Slot 1 now holds CC 1.

steps.title: Assign CC 2 to slot 2
steps.caption: Turn E2 one slot right, press K2, turn E3 to CC 2 and press K3, then K2. Slot 2 now holds CC 2 and slot 1 still holds CC 1.

steps.title: Carry on to slot 5
steps.caption: Repeat for slots 3, 4 and 5 (E2 to the next slot, K2, E3 to the next controller, K3, K2). Slot 5 now holds CC 5.

steps.title: Fill slots 6 to 10
steps.caption: Repeat for CC 6 up to CC 10 on slot 10. All ten slots are now assigned: the list holds CC 1 to CC 10, the most a channel can hold.

steps.title: The first and last slots hold their ends
steps.caption: Select slot 10 and keep turning E2 right: it stops at slot 10. Hold step 1 (1,4) and turn E3 to set the value to 0. Turn E2 left well past slot 1: it stops at slot 1. Hold step 2 (2,4) and set the value to 1. Tap Play (1,8). Before its note, step 1 sends CC 10 and step 2 sends CC 1: look for the two controller changes in the strip below. Tap Play again to stop.

scenes.title: Transpose the next note without cutting the current one

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Press +1 while it plays
steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8) to open the Scale Editor, then tap Play (1,8). One step lasts about a sixth of a second at 90 BPM, so the four-note phrase repeats about every two thirds of a second; exact timing does not matter. While it loops, press (16,8) on the transposition fader once. The screen shows Scale overview with Transpose +1: the note sounding at that moment keeps its pitch and length, and the next notes play a semitone higher, MIDI 61, 63, 65 and 66, as the MIDI strip lists.

steps.title: Press -12 a few notes later
steps.caption: After a few more notes press (9,8) to set -12. Transpose reads -12: again the sounding note is untouched and the next notes drop an octave below the written pitches, 48, 50, 52 and 53.

steps.title: Stop
steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Transpose still reads -12, and in the strip every note-on has its own matching note-off.

steps.title: The whole run
steps.caption: Both edits changed only the next onset: the notes before the first edit are 60, 62, 64, 65, then 61, 63, 65, 66, then 48, 50, 52, 53, and each held note finished at its own pitch and length.

scenes.title: Let a keyboard follow the scale

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the test device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4. The scale is C major, a MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Map scale to white keys is off, its default. The sequencer is stopped, so the keyboard plays the channel's output directly. The norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Raw notes by default
steps.caption: Play the white keys C, D, E, F, G, A, B, then the black keys between them. With Map scale to white keys off every key sends its own pitch: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71 for the white keys, with 61, 63, 66, 68, 70 for the black keys. The strip below lists the notes in the order you played them.

steps.title: Turn the mapping on
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open the MIDI controller options and turn Map scale to white keys On. The row now reads On.

steps.title: White keys follow the scale
steps.caption: Leave PARAMS and play the white keys again. They now follow the selected scale with its root on C: in C major C D E F G A B C sound as 60 62 64 65 67 69 71 72, the same pitches as before. What changes is the black keys: each one repeats the white key above it, so C# sounds 62 instead of 61.

steps.title: Change the scale, change the keys
steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8), turn E3 two detents to change the scale from Major to natural minor and press K3, then tap Channel (3,8). Play the white keys: C D Eb F G Ab Bb C sound as 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72. Black keys still repeat the white key above them: C# plays 62 and D# plays 63. Read the strip below for the thirteen keys C to C: 60 62 62 63 63 65 67 67 68 68 70 70 72, the eight white keys being 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72.

steps.title: Set degree II, rotation 2 and +2
steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Turn E2 once and E3 to set the scale degree to II, press K3, turn E2 three detents and E3 to set rotation 2, press K3, then raise the transposition fader (the minimum at (9,8), then (16,8) fourteen times) to +2. Press Channel (3,8) and play the white keys C to C. All three Honour options are still Off, so the keys follow plain natural minor: look in the strip for 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72, with each black key repeating the white key above it.

steps.title: Honour scale degree
steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > MIDI controller options and turn Honour scale degree On, leave PARAMS and play the keys again. The seven white keys now start on degree II, so the whole run shifts: read the new notes in the strip below.

steps.title: Add rotation
steps.caption: Turn Honour scale rotations On as well and play the keys again. Rotation 2 drops the last two of the seven positions by an octave: compare the strip with the previous step.

steps.title: Add transposition
steps.caption: Turn Honour scale transpose On too and play the keys again. Everything now sounds two semitones higher than in the previous step.

steps.title: Turn mapping off
steps.caption: Turn Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations Off and play, then Honour scale transpose Off, and finally turn Map scale to white keys Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC. Press Channel (3,8) and play C to C: every key plays its own pitch once more, 60 to 72, whatever scale is selected.

scenes.title: Loop a song group or hold one slot

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page; nothing is playing. You build the song in the next step: a two-note motif (MIDI 60, 62) copied into slots 1, 2, 4 and 5, with slots 3 and 6 left empty.

steps.title: Set the global length to 2
steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. The Playback screen reads Global length 2, so every slot plays a two-note motif, 60 and 62.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2 and raise it an octave
steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 will sound 72 and 74.

steps.title: Add slots 4 and 5
steps.caption: Repeat for slot 4, leaving slot 3 empty: copy slot 1 into slot 4 and give it octave +2 at (12,8). Then copy slot 1 into slot 5 and give it octave -1 at (9,8). Slots 3 and 6 stay empty, so there are two groups: slots 1 and 2, and slots 4 and 5.

steps.title: Loop the first group
steps.caption: Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 sounds 60, 62, then slot 2 sounds 72, 74. Slot 3 is empty, so the group ends and playback returns to slot 1: 60, 62, 72, 74, 60, 62, 72, 74. Press Stop.

steps.title: A second group
steps.caption: Tap slot 4 at (4,1) and press Play. Slot 4 sounds 84, 86 and slot 5 sounds 48, 50. Slot 6 is empty, so this second group repeats on its own: 84, 86, 48, 50, 84, 86, 48, 50. Press Stop.

steps.title: Select the next slot while playing
steps.caption: Tap slot 4 at (4,1) and press Play: slot 4 sounds 84, 86. While it plays, press slot 2 at (2,1). The press is queued, not instant. Slot 4 finishes, then slot 2 plays (72, 74) and its group carries on with slot 1 (60, 62) and slot 2 (72, 74). Press Stop; the screen shows where playback ended.

steps.title: Two presses before the boundary
steps.caption: Tap slot 1 and press Play. After the first note, press slot 4 and then slot 5 before slot 1 ends. Slot 1 finishes (60, 62), then the later press wins: slot 5 plays (48, 50), and its group continues with slot 4 (84, 86) and slot 5 again. Press Stop.

steps.title: Turn Song mode off
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS > MOSAIC, find Song mode and turn E3 to Off. The row reads Off.

steps.title: Song mode off holds the slot
steps.caption: Press K2 to leave the menu, select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play. Slot 1 repeats, 60, 62, 60, 62, and does not advance to slot 2. Slot setup shows Song mode Off. Press Stop.

steps.title: Manual selection still works
steps.caption: With Song mode Off, press Play on slot 1, then tap slot 2 at (2,1) while it plays. The press is still queued: slot 1 finishes (60, 62), then slot 2 repeats (72, 74, 72, 74) and keeps repeating. Song Playback reads Song mode MANUAL and Next HOLD.

steps.title: Song mode back on
steps.caption: Turn Song mode On again the same way (PARAMS > MOSAIC), select slot 2 and press Play. Progression resumes inside the group: slot 2 (72, 74), slot 1 (60, 62), slot 2, slot 1.

scenes.title: Foundation and All: who decides the trigs

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the test device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Both patterns are assigned, Add amount is 100 and Add accent is 70. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

steps.title: Open Merge modes
steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge modes and press K3. Strategy reads FOUNDATION: Foundation, not the saved trig merge, is choosing this channel's trigs.

steps.title: Foundation decides the trigs
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Active. Strategy and Active both read FOUNDATION and Pending reads NONE. The Strategy key (14,8) glows at its brightest, the sign that Foundation is in charge: the four anchors on steps 1 to 4 plus additions on steps 5 and 7.

steps.title: Hear Foundation
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. You hear C D E F (60, 62, 64, 65) followed by the additions, a C on steps 5 and 7. Look at the strip below: the additions are quieter, velocity 70, because Add accent 70 scales pattern 2's velocity of 100.

steps.title: Switch the Strategy to All
steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to ALL. Strategy and Active read ALL and the Strategy key (14,8) dims: the saved trig merge is deciding again, with every trig of both patterns.

steps.title: Hear All
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. The same notes sound, but the additions on steps 5 and 7 now keep pattern 2's own velocity, 100, so they are louder than Foundation's 70 in the strip below.

steps.title: Return to Skip
steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED, Strategy and Active read SKIP and the Strategy key (14,8) dims further. Skip, Only and All hand the trigs back to the saved legacy merge; Foundation's protection and accent no longer apply.

scenes.title: Skip and All on a step both patterns trig

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the test device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100) has trigs on steps 3 and 7, so step 3 is a step both patterns trig. Both patterns are assigned. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4 and 7.

steps.title: Open Merge modes
steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge modes and press K3. Strategy reads FOUNDATION: Foundation, not the saved trig merge, is choosing this channel's trigs.

steps.title: Hand the trigs back to Skip
steps.caption: Turn E3 left to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED and the Strategy key (14,8) dims. Skip applies a trig only if it appears in exactly one selected pattern, so step 3, where both patterns trig, will not sound.

steps.title: Hear Skip
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. The strip below lists C D F (60, 62, 65) from pattern 1 on steps 1, 2 and 4, then a C at velocity 100 on step 7, which only pattern 2 trigs. Step 3 is silent: there is no E and no merged note.

steps.title: Switch the Strategy to All
steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to ALL. Strategy and Active read ALL. All applies a trig if it appears in any selected pattern, so step 3 now sounds.

steps.title: Hear All
steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. Step 3 now sounds, merged from both patterns: the Average note merge puts the E (degree III) and the C (degree I) on degree II, a D (62), and the Average velocity merge turns 107 and 100 into 104. Look for D at velocity 104 between 62 and 65 in the strip below; step 7 is still a C at velocity 100.

scenes.title: See a failed voicing and choose a fallback

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on MIDI channel 1: C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 at 90 BPM, rate /1. Harmony is Off with its default registers and Failure fallback SILENCE. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page. This scene shows what happens when a register leaves no room for a note, as it can after you shift a voice into an unusual range.

steps.title: Open the Bass register
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Its list holds Mode, Register, Tone Map, Result and the Entry / Failure row used later. Turn E3 to set Mode to PATTERN, select Register with E2 and press K3.

steps.title: Raise Bass Low to 50
steps.caption: On the Bass rows turn E2 to Low and E3 to set it to 50. The Low row reads 50.

steps.title: Lower Bass High to 50
steps.caption: Turn E2 to High and E3 to set it to 50. The High row reads 50, so the register is now the single note 50.

steps.title: Centre the Bass register on 50
steps.caption: Turn E2 to Centre and E3 to set it to 50. MIDI 50 is a D, so this register holds no C at all. The Centre row reads 50.

steps.title: Send the written C to Bass
steps.caption: Press K3, then E1 back to the Harmony list, select Tone Map with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 so Tone 0, the written C, goes to Bass, and press K3.

steps.title: Hear the silent step
steps.caption: Tap Play for two loops, then Stop. Step 1 is silent while D, E and F sound (MIDI 62, 64, 65 in the strip below), because Bass has no C to play.

steps.title: Open Result
steps.caption: Press E1 to go back to the Harmony list, select Result with E2 and press K3.

steps.title: Read the failure
steps.caption: Read Result for step 1. Status reads NO VOICING RANGE and CH1 reads NO EVENT, because nothing was sent; a Failure details row appears and K3 opens it.

steps.title: Find Entry / Failure
steps.caption: Optional check first: turn E3 to step 5; Status and CH1 read NO EVENT there because the loop has no trig on step 5, which differs from step 1, where an event existed but could not be voiced. Turn Step back to 1, press K2 to return to the list, select Entry and press K3. The Entry / Failure page lists Failure fallback.

steps.title: Choose Legacy
steps.caption: Select Failure fallback and turn E3 once right: it reads LEGACY. Press K3 to apply.

steps.title: Hear the fallback
steps.caption: Tap Play for two loops, then Stop. C D E F return (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): step 1 now plays through its original C instead of falling silent.

steps.title: Confirm Legacy in Result
steps.caption: Reopen Result: step 1 now reads Status LEGACY RANGE and CH1 C3 > C3 (planned > sent), the sign that the written pitch was used on purpose.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, the Song editor holds only slot 1, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.

steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both, and tap slot 2. Slot 2 is selected and bright, slot 1 is lit: slot 2 holds a copy of the melody.

steps.title: Raise the copy by two semitones
steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Press the left end of the transposition fader at (9,8) to set -12, then press (16,8) fourteen times to reach +2. The Scale overview shows Transpose +2 for this slot.

steps.title: Hear the copy
steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. The copy loops D, E, F sharp, G: MIDI 62, 64, 66 and 67 in the strip below.

steps.title: Slot 1 keeps its pitches
steps.caption: Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). Slot 1 still loops C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): the transposition belongs to the copy only. Tap Play to stop.
